record.original_question: Is there a model of computation in which the Invariance Theorem also holds for time complexity?

evidence.quote: Is there any model of computation in which the Invariance Theorem holds true also for the time complexity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In algorithmic information theory, a description method (or interpreter) is a partial computable function f : {0,1}* → {0,1}*. The Kolmogorov complexity of a string x relative to f is C_f(x) = min{|p| : f(p) = x}. The classical Invariance Theorem states that there exists a universal description method U such that for every description method f, there is a constant c_f with
    C_U(x) ≤ C_f(x) + c_f       for all x ∈ {0,1}*.
Thus, up to an additive constant independent of x, the universal complexity C_U is minimal among all C_f.

For a fixed model of computation M (which specifies how programs are executed and how the running time of a program p on input ε producing output x is measured), define a time-bounded complexity
    C^t_{M,f}(x) = min{|p| : f(p) = x and the computation of f on p in model M halts within time t(|x|)},
or, more generally, a complexity measure that simultaneously accounts for program length and running time in M.

Problem. Does there exist a model of computation M and a corresponding notion of time complexity such that an analogue of the Invariance Theorem holds for time complexity? Concretely: is there a model M together with a universal description method U computable in M such that for every description method f computable in M, there exist constants c_f and a function (or constant) bounding the time overhead, with
    C^t_{M,U}(x) ≤ C^{t'}_{M,f}(x) + c_f
for all x, where t and t' differ only by a multiplicative or additive overhead depending on f but not on x? Construct such a model, or prove that no such model exists.
artifact.category_tag: Algorithmic information theory / time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity
artifact.status_search_result: A general search on the invariance theorem for time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity returned background material (e.g., Levin's time-bounded complexity, which penalizes running time additively via log t and admits a form of universality) but no definitive resolution of whether a fully invariance-respecting time complexity exists across models of computation. The question appears to remain open or model-dependent in the algorithmic-information-theory literature.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov complexity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The invariance theorem states that the optimal description language is at least as efficient as any other description language, with some constant overhead.
status_evidence.claim: Standard invariance theorem is for plain (length-based) Kolmogorov complexity; no analogous unconditional statement for time complexity is given.

status_evidence.title: A Brief Introduction to Kolmogorov Complexity (Koucký)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity and Levin complexity, which combines program length with logarithm of running time.
status_evidence.claim: Time-bounded variants such as Levin complexity provide partial analogues, but the invariance issue with respect to time across models is not fully resolved.
